node.title: Re^2: The wonders of Test::More
node.author: syphilis
node.doctext:
ok $exp eq $got or diag explain [$exp, $got];

Yeah, that's not a bad idea.
I don't get much sense from "or diag explain [$exp, $got]" when the variables are Math::MPFR objects: C:\>perl -MMath::MPFR -MTest::More -e "$got=Math::MPFR->new(2); $exp= Math::MPFR->new(2); ok($got != $exp) or diag explain [$exp, $got]; done_testing();" not ok 1 # Failed test at -e line 1. # [ # bless( do{\(my $o = 46472664)}, 'Math::MPFR' ), # bless( do{\(my $o = 46474008)}, 'Math::MPFR' ) # ] 1..1 # Looks like you failed 1 test of 1. but I could instead use something like or warn "$got == $expected" to provide a more meaningful diagnostic.

There's probably quite a few places in my test scripts where this blow-up could occur, but the blow-up only happens with the overloaded "!=" operator, and then only if the test fails.

Cheers,
Rob
